__comment__: MOST REALISTIC TAPE ADHESIVE: Pressure-sensitive adhesive (PSA) 1930s formula – 60% natural rubber (polyisoprene, high MW, cohesive), 35% rosin (abietic acid tackifier, lowers Tg, adds tack), 5% plasticizer (olive oil/tallow, lowers modulus). Dissolved in turpentine or naphtha, coated 20-40um on backing, dried. Peel strength ~3 N/25mm. This is exactly Scotch transparent tape 1930: rubber+rosin+oil on cellulose film. Heating to 120-150C melts rubber and rosin together; oil keeps it soft so it never fully hardens – remains tacky at room temp (viscoelastic).
